definition: A division of a region into cells, one for each site, where each cell holds the points that are closer to its site than to any other site.
One of the given points a Voronoi diagram is built from, such as a shop or a weather station; each site has its own cell.
The region of all points closer to one site than to any other site; its edges lie on perpendicular bisectors of that site and its neighbouring sites.
A boundary between two neighbouring cells; it lies on the perpendicular bisector of their two sites, so every point on it is the same distance from both.
A point where three or more edges meet; it is the same distance from the sites of all the cells that meet there, and no site is closer to it.
Estimating a quantity at a point as the value at its nearest site, so every point in a Voronoi cell gets the value of that cell's site.
Finding the point in a region whose distance to the nearest site is as large as possible; in IB exams the answer is always at a Voronoi vertex where three edges meet.
